messages:
maya: Bringing up gemma-lite-7b on int8. Ran conversion tool v2.1 -> seeing token shadowing around punctuation; summaries truncate and occasionally emit '<unk>' mid-sentence on long contexts. Posting quick logs.

leo: Which tokenizer did you use? was it the original model vocab or our convert-vocab step?

maya: used convert-vocab with collapse-unicode=True. Tokenizer config: pad_id=0, eos_id=2, unk=3. rotary_mode=shared, head_dim=64. Conversion step: `python conv.py --source hf/gemma-lite-7b --out gemma-lite-7b-int8 --quant int8`

rahul: Can you attach sample I/O? Also, does fp16/fp32 baseline from HF run clean?

maya: fp32 baseline (HF original) is clean. Example: input long prompt (~2500 tokens) -> gold summary ends fine. Converted int8 output: "The report concluded that <unk> the data was skewed." Also observed repeated "." sequences after token 2040.

leo: hunch: vocab collapse step might have merged invisible characters causing neighbor token ids to shift; int8 kernels sometimes assume no sentinel collisions. Try diffing vocab indices between src and converted.

maya: ran quick diff: several punctuation tokens changed indices; notable: '.' moved 5 positions, '…' mapped to '.' as expected, but CRLF normalizer collapsed into empty token at id 0 (pad).

eng-ml-bot: scheduled artifact capture for git/conv run (id: g-2026-03-24-03). Please include tokenizer.json and converter.log.

rahul: Important triage steps: 1) run conversion with collapse-unicode=False 2) run unconstrained int8 kernel (no fastpath) to see if kernel assumptions interact with token ids 3) run a short unit test that inserts punctuation at high token indices to reproduce truncation.

maya: tried collapse-unicode=False -> punctuation indices preserved, output drops <unk> but still sees truncation at >2048 sometimes. Perf: int8 latency roughly same as fp16 but quality slightly worse.

leo: That suggests more than token remap. Could be rotary scaling interplay with int8 quant scale clipping for long sequences. Which rotary implementation did the converter pick? (per-head vs shared)

maya: converter forced rotary_mode=shared to match HF artifact. But our runtime expects per-head scaling in int8 fastpath. Will try forcing headwise.

maya: quick test forcing rotary=headwise in model.json -> truncation went away on one run, but another run produced EOS early. Inconsistent.

rahul: Let's capture KV traces + rotary multipliers per-head across time. If int8 quant had symmetric clipping applied differently per-tensor, you can get drift. Also check that pad_id isn't accidentally set to unk in the runtime mapping table.

eng-ml-bot: artifacts uploaded -> /artifacts/g-2026-03-24-03.zip

leo: FYI I'm starting a bisect of the converter: 1) tokenizer normalization changes 2) rotary mapping heuristics 3) int8 fastpath kernel dispatch. Will report back with minimal repro.

maya: Adding an onboard test request: generate 3k token prompt with repeated punctuation, assert no mid-output <unk> and no early-eos. Please add to conversion CI.

rahul: If we find kernel assumption mismatch, plan: a) add runtime guard to reject converted models with rotary_mode mismatch b) add converter lint step to ensure pad/eos/unk indices preserved or explicitly remapped with warning c) add longctx punctuation fuzz test to maintest.

maya: thanks team. Leaving logs and sample prompts in /shared/onboard/gemma-lite-7b/ folder. Will follow up when bisect narrows commit. :v:
